summary: STRATUS Mars Walk is a 2D/3D web app for Gale Crater mission planning with NASA HiRISE data. Set waypoints and exclusion zones, compare low-slope routes against time budgets, and export plans.
details:
How it works

The application uses a cropped NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE digital terrain model and associated orbital imagery. Elevation data support derived slope calculations, terrain visualisation, and route planning on an approximately 2.024-metre grid.

Users select a starting location, science stops, and a return destination. They can adjust walking speed, maximum slope, science-stop duration, mission time, and reserve time. User-defined exclusions prevent routes from crossing selected areas.

An A* routing engine compares shortest-distance and lower-terrain-cost alternatives. Results include distance, ascent, descent, sampled slope, and estimated mission duration. The interface displays terrain, routes, and elevation profiles, and supports downloadable JSON plans and HTML reports.

Scientific objectives and benefits

Our science context includes the sedimentary environments represented by Shaler, Gillespie Lake, and Sheepbed. The application connects exploration destinations with questions about sediment transport, ancient water, and potentially habitable environments.

Its intended benefit is to make relationships between terrain, scientific objectives, and mission constraints easier to understand. It supports educational exploration and demonstrates a transparent approach to planning with planetary data.

Tools and implementation

The deployed interface uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Canvas, and SVG. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, and Uvicorn. Docker packages the application, GitHub stores the deployment source, and Render hosts the frontend and backend together.

Creativity and responsible interpretation

The project combines interactive 2D/3D exploration, route comparison, science references, exclusion zones, and mission budgeting in one interface. Historical environmental references provide context. Global terrain, environmental curves, and suitability scores are labelled simulations.

The application does not provide live Mars weather or operational astronaut safety certification. Named science pins remain provisional, and the terrain cannot resolve every small obstacle or surface-material hazard.

What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered terrain slope, elevation changes, missing data, exclusion zones, walking speed, science-stop duration, return travel, and reserve time. We balanced scientific objectives with terrain difficulty and mission time constraints. We also considered data coverage, resolution, source reliability, and the limitations of historical environmental measurements. To keep the application accessible, we used a small NASA terrain subset and designed interactive 2D and 3D views. Observed data, derived calculations, and simulations are clearly distinguished.



What is the intended impact of the project?

STRATUS Mars Walk aims to make NASA’s planetary data easier to explore and understand. It helps students, researchers, and space enthusiasts examine how terrain, scientific destinations, and mission constraints affect a hypothetical Marswalk. By comparing routes and showing the effects of exclusions and time limits, the project encourages informed decision-making and awareness of uncertainty. It provides an educational prototype and a foundation for future research into exploration planning, with further scientific validation required before operational use.

Public application: https://marswalk-gale-crater.onrender.com/

Source repository: https://github.com/shriram1210/marswalk-gale-crater
